page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-8 is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by AMD EPYC 7B13 processors on the x86_64 architecture. The server allocates 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores with two threads per core. Memory is provisioned at 16 GB, creating a compact 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The CPU configuration includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. The instance includes neither integrated local storage nor hardware GPU acceleration, requiring network-attached storage for persistent disk capacity.

Benchmark evaluation highlights strong single-core execution, with stress-ng single-core performance ranking in the top 25% of measured systems. In contrast, multi-core metrics—including PassMark CPU scores and Geekbench multi-core results—remain within the middle tier. Memory bandwidth achieves 68.67 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 49.73 GB/sec for large block writes. While single-threaded gzip throughput remains stable at 28.22 GB/sec, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression performs below median expectations. Redis operations execute at 8.73 million operations per second, accompanied by a static web serving throughput of 10.6 GB/sec.

By limiting RAM capacity to 2.0 GB per vCPU and omitting bundled NVMe storage, c2d-highcpu-8 maximizes resource allocation toward pure execution cycles without overhead from unused memory. This hardware profile makes the instance well suited for CI/CD compilation jobs, stateless web routing, containerized batch workers, and distributed microservices that demand dedicated CPU threads without large local data sets.
description: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-8 is a compute-optimized virtual machine featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor and 16 GB of system RAM. Utilizing the x86_64 architecture with a lean 1:2 memory-to-core allocation (2.0 GB per vCPU), it prioritizes processor execution over memory footprint. The configuration includes no onboard local storage and no GPU accelerators, using detached network volumes for persistent storage. Benchmark data reflects top-quartile single-core CPU throughput alongside balanced multi-core metrics, 10.6 GB/sec static web serving throughput, and steady memory transfer rates. Although multi-threaded decompression tests reveal lower relative efficiency under specific workloads, its compute density and dedicated thread allocation suit code compilation pipelines, microservices, batch processing, and stateless web serving.
